title: Pancreatlas
bodyHtml:
Pancreatlas

https://www.pancreatlas.org/

Pancreatlas houses comprehensive, accessible imaging datasets derived from the human pancreas, with the goal of facilitating research in diabetes, pancreatitis, pancreatic cancer, and other pancreatic diseases.

Data Types

Microscopy Imaging

Co-detection by imaging (CODEX), Fluorescence immunohistochemistry (IHC), Histology, Immunohistochemistry (IHC), Imaging Mass Cytometry (IMC)

Data and Resources

Explore Pancreatlas datasets through Pancreatlas or PanKbase.

More About the Resource

Imaging experiments generate massive amounts of data, only a subset of which has historically been made accessible or integrated with other modalities. Pancreatlas aims to circumvent this challenge by generating a comprehensive and accessible repository of human pancreatic raw and processed imaging data. Through a scalable, customizable, and user-friendly interface, Pancreatlas facilitates future research of disorders of the pancreas, including diabetes, pancreatic cancer, and pancreatitis.

Pancreatlas consists of over 4,400 unique pancreas-specific biological images curated across ten data collections. Data were generated using tissue from de-identified organ donors (908 unique individuals) studied by several national and international phenotyping consortia. Image modalities include traditional histology, brightfield and fluorescence immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunohistochemistry, and many images are large cross-sectional regions measuring > 100 square millimeters (approximately 500,000-2 million cells per image). The dataset aims to document pancreatic architecture over the human lifespan and represents ages from birth to 79 years. Approximately two-thirds of the data was generated from nondiabetic individuals with the remaining third composed of donors with type 1, type 2, cystic fibrosis-related, neonatal, and atypical diabetes. It is an important and unique reference dataset for the pancreas biology research field, with expression patterns of 70+ proteins visualized by immunohistochemistry, in addition to rich information available from traditional histological imaging.

Standardized integrated metadata annotations allow users to explore the available data by filtering based on parameters such as:

  • Data collection
  • Donor disease status/duration, age, sex, ID
  • Antigen Markers
  • Organ (peripancreatic lymph nodes, non-peripancreatic lymph nodes, pancreas, spleen, thymus)
  • Pancreatic region (body, head, tail, islet)
  • Type of sample processing
  • Imaging modality

More About the Team

Pancreatlas is developed and curated by The Powers and Brissova Research Group at Vanderbilt University Medical Center and Creative Data Solutions at Vanderbilt University. Pancreatlas is led by Co-Scientific Directors Dr. Diane Saunders and Dr. Marcela Brissova and Creative Data Solutions Director Dr. JP Cartailler. Learn more about the full Pancreatlas team here.
